_readme: Authored target placements per range (target-system task T3). Consumed by range/targets/placements.ts, which resolves each entry against the target-type and mount registries and hands scenes a ready-to-build ResolvedPlacement. A range with no entry here gets [] and is unaffected.
_scope: AUTHORED placements only. Computed layouts stay in code — Range A's ladder is derived (buildRack + BTK authored-inputs model) and the ELR Range solves its stations at runtime against the generated tree field. Neither can be expressed here without losing the derivation; both still produce PlateInstance[] the same way. See placements.ts's header.
_units: Distances may be given as distanceYards OR distanceM (exactly one). Sizes are SI metres unless given as widthInches; beam height may be given as beamHeightYards. xOffsetM is lateral offset from the lane centreline, + = right of the shooter.

test-range._note: ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: instanceId is the array index, and ScopeView's test-range branch auto-commits plates[0]. The gong must stay first.
test-range._layout: Everything stays clear of the NO_HILL_CORRIDOR (10 yd wide, 100 yd long) that test-range-config guarantees down the sight line, and clear of the environment's shooterClearM: 18 grass-free circle. The IDPA sits left, the poppers right, so all three are in one sight picture without occluding each other. From the popper star onward, new targets are placed in the ANGULAR frame (mrad off boresight) rather than by metres of lateral offset -- two targets at different distances occlude each other by ANGLE, so metres alone cannot tell you whether a new target hides an old one. See the star's own _note for the worked bands.

targets._note: The original 12in gong, migrated from TEST_RANGE_GONG (task T9a). Every value here reproduces what that const produced: 100 yd, 12in, dead centre, hung at half the 1.2 yd beam. test-range-targets.test.ts asserts field-for-field equality against the old construction.

Stake-mounted IDPA silhouette (owner, task T9b). 18in wide x 30.75in tall. centreYM 1.2876 puts the SHOULDER LINE at 5 ft (1.524 m) above ground — owner spec, 2026-07-31; it was previously staged at 1.05, which drew the shoulders at only 4.22 ft. Feet then sit ~0.90 m up on the stake and the head reaches ~1.67 m, which is how an IDPA target is actually staged: the cardboard is a torso, not a whole body. 1.8 m left of centre keeps it inside the 10 yd corridor's half-width (4.57 m) and well clear of the poppers.

Two poppers sharing one groupId, so COMMIT and resetDownTargets('test-poppers') stand them up together (task T6). 12in wide x 42in tall. NO centreYM: a hinge-stem target is hinged at its own base and stands on the ground, so the height is derived (heightM/2) — owner, 2026-07-31: poppers must sit at or very near ground level.

Hostage-target assembly (Design/Plans, 'IDPA Hostage/No-Shoot Paddle Targets'). Windowed IDPA silhouette + two independently-shootable hostage paddles (top: binary flip; centre: alternating cycle). 3.2 m right of centre, clear of the poppers (max 2.1 m) and inside the corridor half-width (4.572 m). centreYM 1.2876 matches test-idpa-75's shoulder-at-5ft derivation (same default widthM, same aspect). Every placement in this assembly shares distanceYards 60 exactly — ScopeView filters the hittable rack by exact distanceM equality per engagement, so the backing plate and both paddles must resolve to the identical value. No shared groupId: a group's members must share a mount (placements.ts), and this assembly's three members are on three different mounts by design.

Top (head-level) hostage paddle. Rest stop ('left', mount offset 0) sits 0.175 m left of the backing plate's centreline (== the head zone's x); a hit flips it to 'right' (mount offset +0.35 m, landing 0.175 m right of centreline) and back — a SYMMETRIC swing about the head's centre (owner, on device: 'the pivot point should be behind the center of the head... farther out on the right than the left' — the first pass split the 0.35 m swing 0.15/0.20 instead of 0.175/0.175). xOffsetM = plate centreline (3.2) − half the mount's swing (0.175). centreYM was the head zone's own centre (1.586 = backing centreYM + head local y ~0.652 x widthM) until 2026-08-06, when the owner reported the disc CLIPPING THE SHOULDER: at 1.586 the paddle's bottom edge sat at 1.5098 m, 1.4 cm BELOW the silhouette's shoulder line (1.5240 m — the 5 ft shoulder the backing plate's own centreYM is derived from), and the two plates are coplanar, so the overlap z-fought. Owner chose to RAISE it rather than nudge it in z. 1.61 m puts the bottom edge 1 cm clear of that line; above the shoulder the silhouette is only head/neck (half-width 0.0775 m) and this paddle's inner edge is at 0.0988 m, so no overlap is left at either stop. The disc's top now sits 1.3 cm above the plate's top edge, in open air beside the head. Guarded by a test in hostage-paddle.test.ts, not by this note — the shoulder line is invisible in a screenshot.

Centre (torso-level) hostage paddle, sitting behind the backing plate's window when at its rest stop ('center', xOffsetM 0 on the mount). A hit cycles it out to 'right' (+0.33 m), back to 'center', then 'left' (-0.33 m), alternating sides forever (owner: 'this is not reality, can we have it alternate sides?' — see flip.ts). The swing was ±0.15 m until 2026-08-06, which kept the paddle entirely BEHIND the 18in backing plate at both swung stops — so it read as 'only flips behind the main body' and, worse, became unhittable there: game/shot.ts takes the first plate whose zones an impact breaks and has no occlusion concept, so every shot at the swung paddle resolved against the silhouette's body-0/minus-1 instead. ±0.33 m clears the outline by 2.5 cm (one round at ±0.36 read as too far out on device, so the margin shrank, not the requirement — 0.3048 m is a hard floor). See mount-registry.ts's HOSTAGE_CLAMP_3WAY for the full derivation. xOffsetM/centreYM now match the WINDOW's concentric alignment with body-0 (owner, on device: 'it should line up with the center circle in the target') — centreYM derived from the backing plate's centreYM + body-0's local y (~0.117) x widthM. zNudgeM (render-only, see placements.ts) keeps this paddle's mesh from z-fighting with the backing plate's: both sit at the identical distanceM by design (ScopeView's exact-distanceM rack filter), so without a nudge the two coplanar surfaces flicker (owner, on device: 'looks like it's drawing on the same surface... pixelated'). It was +0.05 (5 cm TOWARD the shooter) until 2026-08-06, when the owner corrected the whole mental model: 'the paddles shouldn't flip towards the shooter but away. Technically the paddle is BEHIND the body target. The bullet goes through the center hole, hits the paddle, it flips away from the shooter.' So -0.05 — 5 cm downrange, behind the plate, seen through the window. The sign is not cosmetic: poseFlip swings the paddle downrange, so a positive nudge would sweep it through the backing plate on every strike.

Dueling tree (Design/Plans/dueling-tree-plan.md). Reuses the shipped hostage-paddle flip mechanism unchanged (flip.ts, poseFlip's 180 deg swing-away-from-shooter) — the only new thing here is the ARRANGEMENT: one post carrying 5 paddles, all resting on the same side. POST CENTRELINE: x = -3.0 m (left of the IDPA silhouette at -1.8, whose outline reaches -2.03; the tree's widest [8in] extent runs -3.26..-2.74, leaving 0.71 m clear air; well inside NO_HILL_CORRIDOR's 4.572 m half-width so the terrain under it is flat). ARM DERIVATION: dueling-tree.ts's duelingTreeSwingM(paddleWidthM) = 2 x (paddleWidthM/2 + DUELING_TREE_POST_RADIUS_M[0.0381] + DUELING_TREE_ARM_CLEARANCE_M[0.02]). For the shipped 6in paddle: 2 x (0.0762 + 0.0381 + 0.02) = 0.2686 m stop-to-stop, i.e. a 0.1343 m arm. Rest stop is authored on the LEFT, so xOffsetM = post - arm = -3.0 - 0.1343 = -3.1343 (this file's authored value below). DISTANCE: 80 yd is deliberately exclusive to the tree (gong 100, IDPA 75, hostage assembly 60, poppers 50) — ScopeView filters the hittable rack by exact distanceM equality, so sharing a distance would silently merge the tree into another target's engagement. CENTRES: duelingTreePaddleYM(i) = 1.397 - i x 0.254 (10in pitch, which exceeds even the 8in paddle's diameter so adjacent paddles never overlap), giving 55/45/35/25/15in — chosen so an 8in paddle's top edge (59in) stays 1in under the 60in post top, and its bottom edge (11in) stays clear of the ground. 8in SWAP RECIPE (DT3 — a documented, tested one-minute edit; the tree ships as 6in, this is not currently applied): for ALL FIVE entries below, change widthInches 6 -> 8, mountId 'dueling-tree-arm-6' -> 'dueling-tree-arm-8', and xOffsetM -3.1343 -> -3.1597 (post stays at -3.0; the arm and therefore the rest offset grow with the paddle). zNudgeM is deliberately omitted on every entry here (must stay 0) — unlike the hostage centre paddle, a tree paddle has no coplanar neighbour to z-fight; the post is a solid cylinder with volume, not a flat backing surface.

POPPER STAR (Design/Plans/popper-star.md). Five 10in purple plates on a hub turning 1 rev/10s, plus a fixed 12in hub plate that re-arms them. THE FIRST CONTINUOUSLY-MOVING TARGET IN THE GAME: range/targets/popper-star.ts owns the kinematics, scope/steel-reactions.ts poses the plates AND rewrites plate.position every frame (which is what makes the live hit test and aim-pick track the arms), and TestRangeScene spins the drawn arms from the same scene clock so the two cannot drift. DISTANCE: 90 yd is deliberately exclusive to these six entries -- ScopeView filters the hittable rack by EXACT distanceM equality, so sharing 50 (poppers) / 60 (hostage) / 75 (IDPA) / 80 (tree) / 100 (gong) would silently merge the star into another target's engagement. LATERAL PLACEMENT was chosen in the ANGULAR frame, not in metres, because occlusion between targets at different distances is an angle problem: the occupied bands seen from the eye are tree -43.9..-38.1, IDPA -29.6..-22.9, gong -1.7..+1.7, popper a 27.3..33.9, popper b 42.6..49.3, hostage 50.9..65.7 mrad. The star needs 2 x 0.727/82.296 = 17.66 mrad, and centring it in the +1.67..+27.29 gap gives 14.48 mrad -> hub x = 1.19 m, spanning 5.63..23.29 mrad: 3.96 mrad clear of the gong, 4.00 mrad clear of popper a. Its swept x extent is 0.463..1.917 m, well inside NO_HILL_CORRIDOR's 4.572 m half-width, so the ground under it is flat and NOTHING was removed from the range and no config changed (owner decision D1). HUB HEIGHT 1.20 m: over a revolution the lowest plate rim reaches 0.473 m (clear of the ground) and the highest 1.927 m. THE HUB IS NEVER AUTHORED -- it is RECOVERED as the exact centroid of the five arm positions below (popper-star.ts's starHubFrom; five evenly-spaced arm vectors sum to zero, so there is no residual), and each arm's angle and radius fall out of atan2/hypot against it. That is why these x/y values carry 9 DECIMAL PLACES rather than 3: at 9 dp the columns sum to exactly 5 x 1.19 and 5 x 1.20 and the recovered hub is exact to 2.2e-16, which popper-star.test.ts asserts. Do not round them. zNudgeM is deliberately OMITTED on every entry (must stay 0): unlike the hostage centre paddle no star plate has a coplanar neighbour -- the hub plate sits 0.32 m clear of every arm plate's inner rim (STAR_HUB_CLEARANCE_M), and the boss and arms behind them are already offset downrange by the scene. ORDER: appended at the END, because instanceId is the array index and ScopeView's test-range branch auto-commits plates[0] (the gong must stay first).

The star's hub plate: bolted 12in steel that RE-ARMS the five arms when struck (owner: 'The center plate resets and raises any targets that are down'). It sits at the hub itself, so its xOffsetM/centreYM ARE the hub coordinates the five arms above are authored around -- but nothing reads them as the hub; the hub is recovered from the arms. resetsGroupId names what a hit re-arms, and it lives on the PLACEMENT rather than on the mount so the 'star-hub-reset' mount stays reusable for a second star or a future plate-rack button. NO groupId of its own, and it CANNOT have one: a group's members must share a mount (placements.ts), and this plate is bolted while the arms are knockdowns -- the same constraint the hostage assembly hit. Per owner decision D2 it resets only its own arm group, not every knockdown on the range, so the 50 yd poppers are unaffected.
